title: The chief question: in what the freedom that makes choice free consists; Roman theologians disagree
source_text: XI. Quod autem videtur in hac quaestione praecipuum, illud est in quo proprie posita sit, illa libertas a qua voluntas libera dicitur, & in qua consistit ratio liberi arbitrii. Qua de re non omnino convenit inter Theologos Ecclesiae Romanae. Sed ut discrepantes eorum sententiae melius intelligi possint, primum tenendum est quae sint in Scholis usitatae libertatis acceptiones atque distinctiones.
pass_a_gloss: But what seems chief in this question is that in which that liberty is properly placed by which the will is called free, and in which the essence of free choice consists. On which matter there is not complete agreement among the Theologians of the Roman Church. But that their discrepant opinions may be better understood, it must first be held what are the acceptations and distinctions of liberty used in the Schools.
pass_b_english: The central point of the question appears to be where, strictly, the freedom lies that makes the will called free and in which the essence of free choice consists.
Theologians of the Roman Church are not entirely agreed on this. To make their differing opinions clearer, one must first set out the senses and distinctions of freedom that the schools employ.

choices.why: Kept as in the preceding locus on free choice in general, so the Roman and Reformed accounts are compared in one vocabulary.
